anchor.statement: Lemma 4.4. Fix h ∈ (0, 1/2). For i = 1, 2, let (U i , E i ) be smooth on (0, ∞ ) × [−1, 1], with E i > 0, and suppose the five integrals in (4.15) define smooth functions there, including one-sided η -derivatives at η = ±1. Write H i = √ 2XE i , m i = (M i , I i , J i , S i , C p,i ). Fix one smooth function Π ax ( η ) on [−1, 1] and set Π i (X, η ) = Π ax ( η ) + C p,i (X, η ), Π i (0, η ) = Π ax ( η ), i = 1, 2. Thus the pressures have the same integration constant at the axis; the velocity profiles need not agree near the axis. Define V 0,i by (4.7), Q s,i , N s,i by (4.16), and p s,i , a i , b s,i , T 0,i by (4.11). We use the explicit formulas (4.16), previously derived with C Q = C N = 0. For any of these quantities f , let ∆ f = f 2 − f 1 . Then the following two conclusions hold.

correspondence.note: Part (ii), the estimate (4.17), is stated. Part (i) appears only in pieces: equal fields and histories give equal p_s at a point, and equality of the I-integral propagates beyond X_h; the conclusions for m, Π, V0, a, b_s and T0 are not stated.
